neighbours.label: narrative moment where a character physically turns their head or body to look at someone or something (whipped her head around, turned to face, spun around, looked up at); 'turn' with no change of gaze stays quiet
fire: A branch snapped behind her, and Mara whirled around to see who was following.
The old soldier paused on the stairs and turned to face his daughter.
At the sound of his name the boy twisted around in his seat.
She set down the tray and swung around, startled by the knock.
The captain stopped pacing and turned to look at the frightened crew.
Hearing the door creak, he jerked his head around toward the hallway.
Lena finally lifted her eyes from the letter and looked up at him.
The stranger halted at the gate and slowly turned around to stare at us.
quiet: A branch snapped behind her, and Mara kept walking without a word.
The old soldier paused on the stairs and turned the lamp down low.
At the sound of the bell the boy closed his book and yawned.
She set down the tray and poured the tea, humming to herself.
The captain stopped pacing and sat down heavily on the bench.
The weather turned cold and the leaves turned brown that week.
Lena finally folded the letter and slipped it into her pocket.
The path halted at the gate and slowly turned to mud beyond it.

notes: Card: peaks on ' around', ' to', ' face', ' up', ' at' and Russian 'обернулся' (turned around), always in fiction where someone turns to see. Probes: whipped her head around 0.88, turned to face 0.67, spun around 0.61, glanced over my shoulder 0.30; turned the key 0.14, 'the road turns to gravel' 0.01.
